entries.title: Public works sets out $4.2 million emergency repair plan
entries.content:
Speaking at the site on Bridge Street, Marla Deen, director of Riverbend Public Works, set out a $4.2 million emergency plan to replace the broken main and the half mile of 1931 cast iron pipe around it.

Deen said the section that failed was due for replacement in about two years. The plan brings that work forward, with crews starting tomorrow and Bridge Street expected to reopen in stages over the next three weeks.

The boil-water notice for the Grid stays in place until test results come back clean, which the department expects within three days. Businesses with water damage can ask the chamber of commerce for help with cleanup costs.
entries.author: mreilly

breakout.title: Public works sets out $4.2 million emergency repair plan
breakout.content:
The city will spend $4.2 million to replace the water main that burst under Bridge Street this morning, along with half a mile of aging pipe around it, Marla Deen, director of Riverbend Public Works, said this evening.

Standing beside the fenced-off hole three blocks up from the river, Deen said the money would come from the city's emergency reserve and that work would begin tomorrow morning. The replacement had not been due for about two years.

We can't keep patching pipes that were laid before anyone on this street was born. This one gave us no warning, and the next one won't either.

Marla Deen

A pipe nearly a century old

The main that failed is a 24-inch cast iron line installed in 1931. Deen said inspectors flagged the downtown section as high risk three years ago, but it sat behind other work on the capital plan, including the Grove Avenue main in Ashgrove.

She said the break most likely started as a small crack that widened as pressure rose during the morning peak. By the time crews shut the valves on either side, around 9:40 a.m., the escaping water had undermined roughly 60 feet of road surface.

The plan replaces the failed section and the neighboring pipe for four blocks in each direction with ductile iron, which the department has used for all new mains since the early 2000s.

What it means for downtown

Bridge Street will reopen in stages over the next three weeks. The block around the break will stay closed to traffic until the road is rebuilt, while the outer blocks should reopen to one lane by the weekend. Routes 2, 5 and 9 will keep crossing the river on the Depot Street Bridge, which adds about 10 minutes to each trip, said Lucia Amaro, general manager of Riverbend Transit.

At least six businesses on Bridge Street reported water damage. Delia Marchetti, president of the Halloway County Chamber of Commerce, said the chamber would help owners with insurance claims and cleanup costs.

"Most of these owners can't afford to lose a week, and this took one," Marchetti said. "The least we can do is take the paperwork off their hands."

Boil-water notice stays in place

The boil-water notice for the Grid remains in effect. Residents should bring tap water to a rolling boil for at least one minute before drinking it, cooking with it or using it to brush their teeth. The department expects test results to come back clean within three days.

Bottled water is available at the main library on Courthouse Square until 8 p.m. each day while the notice is in effect. Residents who can't get there can call the city's helpline to arrange a delivery.

Deen said the department will bring a plan to replace the rest of the Grid's cast iron mains, estimated at $28 million over five years, to city officials next month.

posts.title: Live: Bridge Street water main break
Friday night games moved as the Kettle River rises
posts.content:
Coaches across the county scrambled to find new dates for Friday's high school games as the Kettle River left fields in Northgate and along the greenway under water.

Ruth Ambrose, director of Halloway County Emergency Management, said the river should crest by early evening, but Water Street and the greenway will stay closed through the night.

Residents in the floodplain were urged to stay at the fairgrounds shelter until officials confirm it is safe to return. Schools in Northgate will open late tomorrow.

Marla Deen, director of Riverbend Public Works, said her department will review the storm drains on Water Street once the water drops, starting with the low point at Depot Street.

Business owners along Water Street spent the morning moving stock upstairs and setting door barriers in place.
posts.author: hbrennan

posts.title: Schools close across the county as the snow arrives
posts.content:
Every public school in the county will stay closed tomorrow as the winter storm brings heavy snow and freezing rain across the region, Riverbend Public Schools and the Kettleford district said this evening.

After-school activities and evening events are canceled, and Riverbend Public Schools will text families with the following day's schedule by 6 a.m.
